specification.problem: Grover search as a quantum walk on the complete graph with self-loops (N=2^n vertices, one marked vertex w), where each hop (diffusion) operator fails with amplitude eps and acts as identity on the failure branch. Determine how the success probability and optimal iteration count depend on eps and N, with the claim that eps=O(1/sqrt(N)) is needed to keep O(sqrt(N)) runtime.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Tiny instance, n=2..4 search qubits, one marked vertex w, discrete-time walk only, T about (pi/4)sqrt(N) iterations, one oracle placeholder query per step. The hop is modeled as an incoherent-or-coherent eps-mixture of R_s and I using one ancilla per step. The continuous-time version, the physical barrier model, and the proofs are outside the scope.

symbols.meaning: marked vertex, hidden in the oracle
oracle phase flip I-2|w><w|, black box

equations.label: Lossy hop operator
equations.description: Barrier-affected hop: success amplitude times reflection plus failure amplitude times staying put. It is non-unitary on the search register alone, so it needs an ancilla dilation.
equations.abstract_quote: Then the particle has some amplitude of tunneling through the barriers, and some amplitude of staying put.
equations.justification: Tunnel amplitude and stay-put amplitude are modeled as a coherent sum, as stated in the method sketch; the exact form is an assumption.
assumptions: eps is the same at every step

equations.label: Ancilla dilation
equations.description: Ancilla starts in |0>, is rotated, and controls R_s. The ancilla-0 projection of V gives sqrt(1-eps^2)R_s on the search register and the ancilla-1 projection gives eps I, so the ancilla-1 branch is the failure branch and is not recombined.
equations.justification: Standard way to implement a linear combination by dilation. It is a modeling choice, not from the abstract. Using a fresh ancilla per step keeps the branches unmixed, while measuring and resetting gives a mixed-state variant.
assumptions: ancilla fresh per step or reset after each step

equations.label: Walk step and state after T steps
equations.description: Ideal Grover walk at eps=0. With eps>0 the success probability is taken from the ancilla-0 branch or from the full dilated simulation.
equations.justification: Standard Grover iteration with the reflection replaced by H_eps.
assumptions: barrier acts only on the hop, not on the oracle

equations.label: Scaling condition for failure amplitude
equations.description: Claimed dichotomy. It is not derived here. The heuristic is that accumulated failure about T*eps stays O(1) only if eps*sqrt(N)=O(1).
equations.abstract_quote: We prove that the failure amplitude must scale as $O(1/\sqrt{N})$ for search to retain its quantum $O(\sqrt{N})$ runtime; otherwise, it searches in classical $O(N)$ time.
equations.justification: Directly stated in the abstract; the precise theorem statement and constants are unknown.

registers.name: search
registers.role: vertex index, little-endian integer encoding where qubit i is bit i

registers.name: anc
registers.size: 1 per step, or 1 reused with reset
registers.role: hop-failure flag; |1> means the hop failed

specification.initial_state: H on all search qubits gives |s>; ancilla(s) in |0>.

steps.description: Prepare |s> by applying H to all search qubits.
Repeat T times: apply the oracle placeholder U_w to the search register, one query per step.

Apply the lossy hop: Ry(theta) on a fresh ancilla, then R_s on the search register controlled on ancilla=0 (H, X, multi-controlled Z, X, H, with the control added). Note that controlled-R_s applied exactly equals a controlled global-phase-corrected reflection, so the controlled version must keep the correct relative phase, for example by controlling only the central multi-controlled Z. Then reset or discard the ancilla.
Sweep T and eps, using eps=c/sqrt(N) and eps=const, to find max P(w) and optimal T versus N.

specification.measurement: Measure the n search qubits, with the little-endian bit order of counts keys taken into account. The most frequent outcome estimates w. Optionally postselect on all ancillas=0.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Take the argmax of the counts, or compute P(w) from the statevector. Determine the optimal T and max P(w) for each N and eps.
assumptions: Complete graph with self-loops, single marked vertex
Ancilla per step is within the qubit cap, otherwise reset is used
missing_information: Exact hop-failure model used in the paper, coherent versus incoherent
The proof and constants for the eps scaling
Continuous-time Hamiltonian and barrier-reduced hopping amplitude
Qubit cap and query budget values
